title: console-surge-lite-mode-mvp-scope-reduction-and-acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Rebaseline Console MVP to a "Lite/Surge" surface that preserves core cost breakdown and basic trace linking while deferring higher-cardinality dashboards and realtime trace detail. This change reduces scope to accelerate a safe alpha release for internal beta customers and to lower telemetry costs during the MVP window.
background: Initial PRD targeted a broad set of dashboard cards, full per-route tracing drilldowns, and a rich cost-explorer. After dev estimates and early infra capacity tests we hit two constraints: (1) telemetry ingestion cost projections exceed budget for MVP under expected beta load, and (2) trace indexing for full-span search requires infra components we cannot onboard reliably before the release date. PM/Eng/Design agreed to a scoped 'Surge Lite' approach to ship a smaller, usable surface with clear fallbacks.
proposed_scope: Compact Route Cost Card (top 10 routes by spend, 7-day delta, percent change)
Cost Breakdown Summary per model and per-route (aggregated metrics, no per-request drilldown)
Trace Link from a route card to a sampled recent trace (sample rate configurable to 0.5% by default)
Errors & Latency mini-card (p95, error-rate) with time-series sparkline, 24h and 7d views
A single consolidated Insights page containing the above cards and an export CSV button
Basic rollout flags to enable/disable the full telemetry surface per customer tier
removed_scope: High-cardinality dashboard tiles (per-model+per-route breakdowns beyond top 10)
Realtime trace explorer with span-level search and filtering
Long-retention cost attribution and multi-dimensional grouping UI
Automated anomaly detection and alerting for cost regressions (deferred to post-MVP)
rationale_for_cuts: Reduce telemetry ingestion and storage cost to meet MVP budget constraints
Minimize infra surface to avoid runway risk — defer trace indexing until stable ingestion is in place
Deliver a usable product that surfaces actionable insights (top spenders and regressions) rather than a broad but shallow set of tiles
Keep the alpha release small for product-led onboarding and easier support during early customer feedback
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Compact Route Cost Card shows top 10 routes by total spend over the last 7 days and supports 24h/7d toggles
AC-2: Cost Breakdown Summary displays aggregated cost by model and by route (no more than 10 entries each) and can be exported as CSV

AC-3: Trace Link opens a sampled trace for the selected route where sampling rate is configurable and defaults to 0.5% in prod; when sampling is 0% the UI shows a 'trace not available' fallback message
AC-4: Error & Latency mini-card reports p95 and error-rate with data freshness <= 2 minutes for rolling 24h window under standard load
AC-5: UI falls back gracefully when telemetry is throttled: cards show last-known values and a banner explaining limited telemetry; feature flag controls must allow disabling the surface per-customer
AC-6: End-to-end test coverage for the main Insights page exists (integration test hitting a mocked telemetry service) and passes in CI
AC-7: Alpha rollout to internal beta customers should not increase telemetry costs above the approved budget threshold for MVP (tracked by cost dashboard)
AC-8: Product acceptance signoff from Eng, Design, and Support recorded in the PRD thread
tradeoffs: Lower sampling reduces trace availability for debugging production incidents — we accept fewer traces to keep cost down
Less detailed dashboards limit deep investigation by early customers; will rely on support-run diagnostics and targeted bugfixes
Deferring anomaly detection means manual monitoring/triage will be required initially
Keeping export CSV only (no interactive drilldown) reduces developer work but may increase ad-hoc support requests
open_questions: Q1: Should the default trace sampling be 0.5% or 1% for internal alpha? Engineering suggests 0.5% meets budget but 1% materially improves debugging signals
Q2: For customers that opt-in to higher telemetry, what guardrails (rate limits, billing alerts) should we surface in the UI?
Q3: Do we need a temporary support playbook for common investigations given reduced trace availability?
Q4: Are there specific enterprise customers expecting per-request cost breakdowns in the first release that we need to call out as exceptions?

2026-03-11: Engineering confirmed sampling plumbing is ready for 0.5% default; opted for a feature flag to increase sample rate for internal beta (Liam C.)
2026-03-13: Design signoff on compact card visual language and fallback messaging (Maya S.)
2026-03-14: Support provided draft playbook for degraded playback of traces; requires final review (Jorge M.)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature flags and basic UI deployed to staging with mocked telemetry (2026-03-18)
Stage 1: Internal alpha deploy to SRE and product teams with sampling at 1% for two days to validate UX (2026-03-20)
Stage 2: Toggle sampling to 0.5% and open alpha to small set of beta customers (by invitation) with support playbook (2026-03-22)
Stage 3: Monitor telemetry cost and user feedback for two weeks before deciding post-MVP features (2026-04-05 decision checkpoint)
qa_notes: Integration tests should include a throttled telemetry scenario to validate fallback banner and last-known-value behavior
Simulate high-cardinality traffic in staging to ensure UI gracefully limits to top 10 without errors
Validate CSV export includes correct aggregation and timestamps in UTC
Verify feature flags successfully disable entire Insights page and per-card controls behave as expected

2026-03-12: Eng provided updated estimates; moved per-request cost to post-MVP
2026-03-13: Design delivered compact card comps and fallback copy; UX review passed
2026-03-14: Support draft playbook shared; requested examples of common triage flows
2026-03-15: PM consolidated acceptance criteria and opened this ticket for review
post_mvp_backlog: Onboard full trace indexing and span-level search
Anomaly detection for cost regressions and automated alerts
notes_for_engineering: Prioritize stable fallback states and feature-flagging. Keep telemetry schema changes backwards-compatible. Instrument a tight budget dashboard to track ingestion cost in real-time for the alpha rollout.
